nodes.name: Query
nodes.statement: A \emph{query} is a measurable space representing the possible outcomes of asking a single question or making a single observation.
differentia: representing the possible outcomes of asking a single question or making a single observation
nodes.label: def:query

nodes.name: Refinement
nodes.statement: A \emph{refinement} between queries is a measurable function showing how outcomes of one query determine outcomes of another.
differentia: showing how outcomes of one query determine outcomes of another
nodes.label: def:refine

nodes.name: Query system
nodes.statement: A \emph{query system} is a preordered family of queries with coherent refinement maps. It consists of: \begin{itemize} \item An index type $\iota$ \item A family of queries $q : \iota \to \text{Query}$ \item A preorder relation $\le$ on indices \item Refinement maps $\pi : \forall \{i\ j\}, i \le j \to \text{Refine}(q_i, q_j)$ \end{itemize} subject to functoriality conditions.
nodes.statement_short: Index type with a preorder, a family of queries and functorial refinement maps between comparable indices.
also_stated_at: This formalization develops query systems: preordered families of measurable spaces with compatible refinement maps.
nodes.label: def:query-system

nodes.name: Projective limit
nodes.statement: The \emph{projective limit} $\Omega$ is the space of coherent families of query outcomes. An element $\omega : \Omega$ assigns to each query $i$ an outcome $\omega(i)$, subject to the coherence condition: whenever $i \le j$, we have $\omega(j) = \pi_{ij}(\omega(i))$.
nodes.genus: space of coherent families of query outcomes
nodes.statement_short: Ω consists of outcome assignments ω(i) coherent under refinement maps.
nodes.label: def:omega

nodes.name: Cylinder set
nodes.statement: A \emph{cylinder set} $\text{Cyl}(i, A)$ is the set of realizations where query $i$ yields an outcome in $A$. These generate the observable $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.label: def:cylinder

nodes.name: Compatible marginals
nodes.statement:
A family $
u$ of measures on query outcomes is \emph{compatible} if the measures commute with refinement maps: whenever $i \le j$, the pushforward of $
u_i$ along $\pi_{ij}$ equals $
u_j$.
nodes.label: def:compatible-marginals

nodes.name: Upper-directed
nodes.statement: A query system is \emph{upper-directed} if any two queries have a common refinement: $\forall i\,j, \exists k, i \le k \land j \le k$.
nodes.label: def:upper-directed

nodes.name: Sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: Every \emph{sequence} of queries has a common refinement: $\forall u : \mathbb{N} \to \iota, \exists k, \forall n, u_n \le k$. Strictly stronger than upper-directedness, which bounds pairs. It says the completed query $\bigvee_n Q_n$ is itself a query.
nodes.statement_short: Every sequence of indices has a common upper bound, strictly stronger than pairwise upper-directedness.
nodes.label: def:seq-upper-directed

nodes.name: Surjective evaluations
nodes.statement: Every evaluation $\mathrm{eval}_i : \Omega \to \mathrm{Outcome}_i$ is surjective: each local outcome extends to a coherent global realization. It gives $\mathrm{Cyl}_k E_1 = \mathrm{Cyl}_k E_2 \Rightarrow E_1 = E_2$.
nodes.label: def:eval-surjective

nodes.name: Cylinders form a pi-system
nodes.statement: Under upper-directedness, the cylinder family forms a $\pi$-system.
conclusions: the cylinder family forms a $\pi$-system
nodes.label: lem:pi-system

nodes.name: Proof of lem:pi-system
nodes.statement: Upper-directedness gives a common refinement of any two cylinder-generating queries; intersect the pulled-back events there.
nodes.statement_short: Common refinement of two cylinder-generating queries; intersect pulled-back events there.

nodes.name: Observational Determination
nodes.statement: Two (finite) measures on the projective limit $\Omega$ are equal if and only if they have equal marginals on all queries, i.e.\ equal pushforwards along every $\mathrm{eval}_i$. No compatibility hypothesis is consumed.
equivalent_conditions: Two (finite) measures on the projective limit $\Omega$ are equal
they have equal marginals on all queries
conclusions: Two (finite) measures on the projective limit $\Omega$ are equal if and only if they have equal marginals on all queries
nodes.label: thm:observational-determination

nodes.name: Proof of Observational Determination
nodes.statement: Apply the $\pi$-$\lambda$ theorem to the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra. The cylinders form a $\pi$-system by \ref{lem:pi-system}, and the hypothesis gives agreement on all cylinders.
nodes.statement_short: Pi-lambda theorem on the cylinder σ-algebra, cylinders being a π-system.

nodes.name: Premeasure Well-Definedness
nodes.statement: The premeasure defined on finite cylinders is well-defined: it doesn't depend on the choice of common \emph{upper} bound (refinement level) used in its definition.
conclusions: The premeasure defined on finite cylinders is well-defined
nodes.label: lem:premu-well-defined

nodes.name: Proof of Premeasure Well-Definedness
nodes.statement: Given two upper bounds, use upper-directedness to find a common refinement of both. Show the measure values agree using compatibility and proof irrelevance for the transitivity witnesses.
nodes.statement_short: Take a common refinement of two upper bounds and compare values via compatibility.

nodes.name: Stone space of a query system
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{St}(S)$ is the space of ultrafilters on $\Omega$, i.e. the Stone--\v{C}ech compactification of $\Omega$ regarded as a discrete set. It is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:stone-space

nodes.name: Cylinder clopens
nodes.statement: The sets $\{u : E \in u\}$ for $E$ a cylinder event. These are clopen, form a set semiring, and generate the $\sigma$-algebra used on $\mathrm{St}(S)$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:stone-clopens

nodes.name: Normalized compatible contents
nodes.statement: A family $\nu_i$ of finitely additive contents on the outcome spaces, compatible under refinement, each of total mass $1$. Finitely additive only.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.genus: family $\nu_i$ of finitely additive contents on the outcome spaces
nodes.label: def:ncc

nodes.name: Collective exhaustion
nodes.statement: For every index $i$ and every decreasing sequence of measurable events shrinking to $\emptyset$, some finer level $j \geq i$ witnesses convergence: the charge of the pulled-back sequence at $j$ tends to $0$. Index-layer conditions do not suffice (\texttt{counterexampleQS\_no\_finitary\_condition}).
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.statement_short: For every level and every decreasing sequence shrinking to empty, some finer level's charges of the pulled-back sequence tend to 0.
nodes.label: def:collectively-exhaustive

nodes.name: Collective exhaustion is per-level $\sigma$-additivity
nodes.statement: $\nu$ is collectively exhaustive if and only if every $\nu_i$ is continuous at $\emptyset$, i.e. $\sigma$-additive.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
conclusions: $\nu$ is collectively exhaustive if and only if every $\nu_i$ is continuous at $\emptyset$, i.e. $\sigma$-additive
nodes.label: lem:ce-levelwise

nodes.name: Proof of Collective exhaustion is per-level $\sigma$-additivity
nodes.statement: Compatibility gives $\nu_i(A) = \nu_j(\pi^{-1}A)$ outright, so the quantity tested at the finer level $j$ is equal to the one at $i$ and the existential in \ref{def:collectively-exhaustive} is cosmetic.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility makes the charge at a finer level equal the one at the base level, so the existential is cosmetic.

nodes.name: SP1
nodes.statement: Collective exhaustion holds if and only if every level's content extends to a genuine measure on that level's outcome space.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
equivalent_conditions: every level's content extends to a genuine measure on that level's outcome space
conclusions: Collective exhaustion holds if and only if every level's content extends to a genuine measure on that level's outcome space
nodes.label: thm:sp1-iff

nodes.name: Proof of SP1
nodes.statement: By \ref{lem:ce-levelwise} collective exhaustion is continuity at $\emptyset$ of each $\nu_i$, which for a content on a $\sigma$-algebra is countable additivity.
nodes.section: 2.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.statement_short: Via the per-level lemma: continuity at ∅ of a content on a σ-algebra is countable additivity.

nodes.name: Observational extension, sequential form
nodes.statement: If $S$ is \emph{sequentially} upper-directed with surjective evaluations and $\nu_i$ is a compatible family of probability \emph{measures}, then there is a unique probability measure $P$ on $\Omega$ with $\mathrm{map}(\mathrm{eval}_i)\,P = \nu_i$ for every $i$.
assumptions: $\nu_i$ is a compatible family of probability \emph{measures}
conclusions: there is a unique probability measure $P$ on $\Omega$ with $\mathrm{map}(\mathrm{eval}_i)\,P = \nu_i$ for every $i$
nodes.statement_short: Sequential upper-directedness plus surjective evaluations: compatible probability marginals extend uniquely to a measure on Ω.
nodes.label: thm:observational-extension-seq

nodes.name: Proof of Observational extension, sequential form
nodes.statement: Carath\'eodory on the cylinder semiring. Build the cylinder content --- its value on a cylinder is \texttt{pre}$\mu$ at a singleton presentation, so \ref{lem:premu-well-defined} is what makes the content well defined --- prove $\sigma$-subadditivity (\ref{lem:cylgen-sigma-subadd}), extend, recover marginals; uniqueness is \ref{thm:observational-determination}.
nodes.statement_short: Carathéodory on the cylinder semiring: well-defined content, σ-subadditivity, extension, uniqueness by determination.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-subadditivity from a common upper bound
nodes.statement: Under sequential upper-directedness (with surjective evaluations and compatible marginal measures) the cylinder content is $\sigma$-subadditive.
assumptions: Under sequential upper-directedness (with surjective evaluations and compatible marginal measures)
conclusions: the cylinder content is $\sigma$-subadditive
nodes.label: lem:cylgen-sigma-subadd

nodes.name: Proof of $\sigma$-subadditivity from a common upper bound
nodes.statement: Sequentiality is used exactly once: given a countable cover, it produces a \emph{single} index $m$ above every index appearing in it, after which $\sigma$-subadditivity of the one measure $\nu_m$ finishes the argument. Ordinary upper-directedness bounds \emph{pairs} of indices, not countable families, so no single $\nu_m$ dominates a countable cover; with ordinary upper-directedness plus collective exhaustion in place of sequentiality this lemma is \textbf{false}, by the Andersen--Jessen system of \S\ref{sec:sequentiality}.
nodes.statement_short: Sequentiality gives one index above a countable cover; σ-subadditivity of that single marginal finishes.

nodes.name: Observational extension from charges
nodes.statement: For a \emph{sequentially} upper-directed query system with surjective evaluations and a collectively exhaustive normalized compatible family $\nu$ of finitely additive charges, there is a unique probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ with $\mu(\mathrm{Cyl}_i A) = \nu_i(A)$ for every query $i$ and measurable $A$.
assumptions: a \emph{sequentially} upper-directed query system with surjective evaluations
a collectively exhaustive normalized compatible family $\nu$ of finitely additive charges
conclusions: there is a unique probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ with $\mu(\mathrm{Cyl}_i A) = \nu_i(A)$ for every query $i$ and measurable $A$
nodes.statement_short: Collectively exhaustive compatible finitely additive charges on a sequentially upper-directed system extend uniquely to a probability measure.
nodes.label: thm:stone-observational-extension

nodes.name: Proof of Observational extension from charges
nodes.statement: \ref{thm:sp1-iff} converts collective exhaustion into a genuine measure at each level; compatibility transfers because each $\mu_i$ agrees with $\nu_i$ on every measurable set; and \ref{thm:observational-extension-seq} finishes on $\Omega$, its uniqueness clause included.
nodes.statement_short: Turn collective exhaustion into per-level measures (SP1), then apply the sequential extension theorem.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov extension fails under plain upper-directedness
nodes.statement:
Drop sequentiality to plain upper-directedness and the hypotheses of
\ref{thm:stone-observational-extension} read, via \ref{lem:ce-levelwise}:
compatible marginals, each $\sigma$-additive, plus upper-directedness and
surjective evaluations. That is Kolmogorov extension with no regularity or
compactness hypothesis of any kind --- the outcome spaces carry only a
$\sigma$-algebra --- and it is false.
nodes.origin_citation: Sparre Andersen and Jessen 1948; Border, Kolmogorov Extension Problem, Prop. 17
assumptions: compatible marginals, each $\sigma$-additive, plus upper-directedness and surjective evaluations
conclusions: it is false
nodes.statement_short: With only upper-directedness, compatible σ-additive marginals and surjective evaluations, Kolmogorov extension fails.

nodes.name: Andersen--Jessen counterexample
nodes.statement:
The Andersen--Jessen construction
(Sparre Andersen and Jessen 1948; exposition in K.~C.~Border,
\emph{Kolmogorov Extension Problem}, Prop.~17, following Halmos
\emph{Measure Theory} pp.~68--70) instantiates every hypothesis and refutes
the conclusion.

\emph{The construction.} Take $X_k \subseteq [0,1]$ \emph{thick} --- full
outer measure --- and decreasing with $X_k \downarrow \emptyset$. Thickness
makes $\Sigma_k = \{E \cap X_k : E \text{ Lebesgue measurable}\}$ with
$\lambda_k(E \cap X_k) = \lambda(E)$ a well defined \emph{$\sigma$-additive}
probability space. Index by $\mathbb{N}$ under $\leq$; put
$\mathrm{Outcome}_n = X_0 \times \cdots \times X_n$ with the projections as
bonding maps, so $\Omega = \prod_k X_k$; define $P_n$ by pushing $\lambda_n$
forward along the diagonal $x \mapsto (x,\dots,x)$. These are Kolmogorov
consistent.

\emph{The refutation.} The diagonal cylinders
$D_n = \{(x,\dots,x) \times \prod_{k>n} X_k : x \in X_n\}$ have
$P(D_n) = \lambda_n(X_n) = 1$ for every $n$, while $\bigcap_n D_n = \emptyset$
because $X_k \downarrow \emptyset$. No measure gives every term of a
decreasing sequence mass $1$ and the limit mass $0$.

\emph{Every hypothesis holds.} $\mathbb{N}$ is a chain, hence upper-directed,
and \emph{not} sequentially upper-directed, since $(0,1,2,\dots)$ has no upper
bound. Every $\mathrm{eval}_n$ is a projection onto an initial segment, hence
surjective (each $X_k$ is thick, so nonempty). Each $P_n$ is a genuine measure,
so collective exhaustion holds by \ref{lem:ce-levelwise}. Note $\Omega$ is the
subtype of \emph{coherent} families, not the bare product --- surjectivity onto
a projective limit can fail with every level nonempty --- but the bonding maps
are initial-segment restrictions, so coherence is automatically satisfiable and
nonemptiness of each $X_k$ suffices.
nodes.statement_short: Andersen-Jessen construction: thick decreasing sets X_k with empty intersection, diagonal marginals. Diagonal cylinders have mass 1 but empty intersection.

nodes.statement:
The Andersen--Jessen construction

nodes.name: Failure lives between levels
nodes.statement:
So the failure lives entirely in the passage between levels, where a per-level
condition cannot see it: collective exhaustion characterises $\sigma$-additive
extensibility \emph{per level} (\ref{thm:sp1-iff}) and not globally. The
alternative to assuming sequentiality is a compact-class or perfect-measure
condition on the marginals (Marczewski), the classical hypothesis.

nodes.name: The Stone measure exists and extends the content
nodes.statement: There is a probability measure $\hat P$ on $\mathrm{St}(S)$ with $\hat P(E) = m(E)$ for every cylinder clopen $E$, where $m$ is the additive content transferred from $\nu$ along the Stone embedding. No collective exhaustion and no directedness beyond upper is used.
nodes.section: 2.4 The finitely additive theorem on the Stone space
conclusions: There is a probability measure $\hat P$ on $\mathrm{St}(S)$ with $\hat P(E) = m(E)$ for every cylinder clopen $E$
nodes.statement_short: On the Stone space the transferred content extends to a probability measure, without collective exhaustion.
nodes.label: thm:stone-measure-exists

nodes.name: Proof of The Stone measure exists and extends the content
nodes.statement: Transfer $\nu$ to an additive content on the cylinder clopens; prove $\sigma$-subadditivity using compactness of the Stone space (every countable cover of a clopen has a finite subcover); apply Carath\'eodory.
nodes.section: 2.4 The finitely additive theorem on the Stone space
nodes.statement_short: Transfer content to clopens, σ-subadditivity by compactness of the Stone space, then Carathéodory.

nodes.name: Escaping tower
nodes.statement: A decreasing sequence of cylinder events, each of full charge, with empty intersection.
nodes.label: def:escaping-tower

nodes.name: No extension over an escaping tower
nodes.statement: A query system carrying an escaping tower admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$. No hypotheses on $S$ are used --- no directedness, no surjectivity, no collective exhaustion.
assumptions: A query system carrying an escaping tower
conclusions: admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$
nodes.label: thm:no-extension-tower

nodes.name: Proof of No extension over an escaping tower
nodes.statement: The tower's cylinders are an antitone measurable sequence with empty intersection and every stage of mass $1$, which is exactly what \ref{lem:cont-above} forbids.
nodes.statement_short: Tower cylinders contradict continuity from above.

nodes.name: The obstruction is not vacuous
nodes.statement: The finite--cofinite query system carries an escaping tower: with $E_n = \mathbb{Q} \setminus \{q_0,\dots,q_n\}$, each $E_n$ is cofinite hence in the hyperfilter hence of content $1$, while $\bigcap_n E_n = \emptyset$.
conclusions: The finite--cofinite query system carries an escaping tower
nodes.label: thm:tower-inhabited

nodes.name: Proof of The obstruction is not vacuous
nodes.statement: Direct.
nodes.statement_short: Direct verification.

nodes.name: The finite--cofinite system admits no extension
nodes.statement: The finite--cofinite query system admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$. It fails collective exhaustion (\texttt{counterexampleNCC\_not\_collectivelyExhaustive}), so it does not refute the plain-upper-directedness extension statement of \S\ref{sec:sequentiality}.
conclusions: The finite--cofinite query system admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$.
It fails collective exhaustion
nodes.label: cor:cex-no-extension

nodes.name: Proof of The finite--cofinite system admits no extension
nodes.statement: Instantiate \ref{thm:no-extension-tower} at the finite--cofinite escaping tower of \ref{thm:tower-inhabited}.
nodes.statement_short: Instantiate the escaping-tower obstruction at the finite-cofinite tower.

nodes.name: Finiteness rather than parity
nodes.statement:
The tower is built from \emph{finiteness} rather than the parity split of the
source (Border, following Halmos pp.~68--70). Parity caps out: a set with all
even differences lies in a coset of $2\mathbb{Z}+\alpha\mathbb{Z}$, of which
there are two, so it can never separate more than two pieces and gives
thickness only at $k = 0$. A finite set has no such cap, and
\ref{thm:aj-finite} gives thickness at every level.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.statement_short: The parity split of the classical source yields thickness only at k=0; finite translates give thickness at every level.

nodes.name: The group
nodes.statement: $A = \mathbb{Z} + \alpha\mathbb{Z}$ for $\alpha$ irrational (as a set, and as the additive subgroup \texttt{Afull} of $\mathbb{R}$). Countable.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: def:aj-A

nodes.name: Density
nodes.statement: $A$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
conclusions: $A$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.label: lem:aj-dense

nodes.name: Proof of Density
nodes.statement: $2\mathbb{Z}+\alpha\mathbb{Z}$ is a subgroup, so by \texttt{AddSubgroup.dense\_or\_cyclic} it is dense or cyclic; a generator $g$ would give $2 = pg$ and $\alpha = qg$, making $\alpha = 2q/p$ rational. Density of $A$ follows by monotonicity.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.statement_short: A subgroup of R is dense or cyclic; cyclicity would make α rational.

nodes.name: Proof of Finiteness beats parity
nodes.statement: If it did, Steinhaus (\texttt{Measure.sub\_mem\_nhds\_zero\_of\_addHaar\_pos}) puts a neighbourhood of $0$ inside $F' - F'$. $F - F$ is finite while $A$ is dense, so some element of $A$ lies in that neighbourhood and outside $F - F$; the transversal then forces it into $F - F$ after all.

nodes.name: The thick tower
nodes.statement: With $A$ enumerated, set $X_k = V + \{a_j : j \geq k\}$. Then $X_k$ is decreasing (\texttt{X\_antitone}), $\bigcap_k X_k = \emptyset$ (\texttt{X\_iInter}), and every $X_k$ is thick: any measurable set disjoint from it is null.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
assumptions: With $A$ enumerated, set $X_k = V + \{a_j : j \geq k\}$.
conclusions: $X_k$ is decreasing
$\bigcap_k X_k = \emptyset$
every $X_k$ is thick: any measurable set disjoint from it is null
nodes.statement_short: The tails V + {a_j : j ≥ k} form a decreasing tower of thick sets with empty intersection.

nodes.name: Proof of The thick tower
nodes.statement: $X_k^c = V + \{a_0,\dots,a_{k-1}\}$, a finite subset of $A$, so \ref{thm:aj-finite} applies at every $k$. The empty intersection needs only the enumeration covering $A$ and the transversal property (\ref{lem:aj-V}): each real decomposes as $v + a$ with $v$ forced, and $a$ eventually falls out of every tail.
nodes.section: 3 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.statement_short: Complements are finite translates, so thickness follows from finiteness-beats-parity; emptiness from the transversal.

nodes.name: Thickness, relative to a base measure
nodes.statement: $X$ is \emph{thick for} $\mu$ when every measurable set disjoint from $X$ is $\mu$-null. The base is arbitrary rather than Lebesgue because the marginals need mass $1$ and $\lambda(\mathbb{R}) = \infty$, while $X_k \cap [0,1]$ is not thick in $\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.statement: For $X$ thick for $\mu$, the traces $\{E \cap X\}$ carry a measure with $\lambda_X(E \cap X) = \mu(E)$ (Border, Prop.~14).

nodes.name: Proof of The trace measure on a thick set

Well-definedness is where thickness is spent --- two measurable sets with the same trace differ by a measurable set disjoint from $X$, hence null --- and $\sigma$-additivity follows because disjoint traces force a.e.-disjoint representatives.

conclusions: The Andersen--Jessen query system carries compatible $\sigma$-additive probability marginals and admits no extension to a probability measure on $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Proof of Andersen--Jessen admits no extension
nodes.statement: The levels carry trace measures (\ref{thm:trace-measure}) over the restricted base, so each is a probability measure, and they are compatible along the tower's inclusions. Pushing them along the diagonal gives Kolmogorov-consistent marginals; the commutation $\mathrm{bond} \circ \mathrm{diag} = \mathrm{diag} \circ \mathrm{incl}$ is definitional. The diagonal cylinders then form an escaping tower: each carries full mass because the diagonal map lands in the diagonal, and their intersection is empty by \ref{thm:diag-empty}. A coherent family is not a sequence, so it is carried to one by $\mathrm{toSeq}\,\omega : k \mapsto (\omega_k)_k$, reading off the top coordinate at each level. Every entry lies in its own $X_k$ by the subtype alone, while constancy needs both the coherence (to move coordinate $0$ down from level $i$ to level $0$) and the base cylinders (to move it across level $i$ from coordinate $0$ to coordinate $i$). \ref{thm:diag-empty} then supplies the emptiness, against \ref{thm:aj-tower}, and \ref{thm:no-extension-tower} finishes.
nodes.section: 3.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.statement_short: Trace measures pushed along the diagonal give consistent marginals whose diagonal cylinders form an escaping tower. The key step: coherent families are constant, so the diagonal escapes.

nodes.name: Diagonal cylinders
nodes.statement: $D_n = \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0 \text{ for all } i \leq n\}$ inside $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with the product $\sigma$-algebra, and $\Pi'(Y) = \{\omega : \omega_k \in Y_k \text{ for all } k\}$ (\texttt{Pi'}). The cylinders decrease (\texttt{Diag\_antitone}), and a point of $D_n$ is determined on $[0,n]$ by its first coordinate (\texttt{Diag\_eq\_of\_le}).
nodes.label: def:diag-cylinders

nodes.name: The cylinders shrink to the constants
nodes.statement: $\bigcap_n D_n = \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0 \text{ for all } i\}$: the sequences that are constant outright.
conclusions: $\bigcap_n D_n = \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0 \text{ for all } i\}$
nodes.label: lem:diag-inter

nodes.name: Proof of The cylinders shrink to the constants
nodes.statement: Both inclusions are immediate from the definition; the forward one reads off the bound $i \leq n$ at $n = i$.
nodes.statement_short: Both inclusions immediate from the definition.

nodes.name: The diagonal escapes
nodes.statement: If $\bigcap_k Y_k = \emptyset$ then $\Pi'(Y) \cap \bigcap_n D_n = \emptyset$, generically in $Y$.
conclusions: $\Pi'(Y) \cap \bigcap_n D_n = \emptyset$
nodes.label: thm:diag-empty

nodes.name: Proof of The diagonal escapes
nodes.statement: A point of every $D_n$ is constant by \ref{lem:diag-inter}, so its common value $\omega_0$ lies in $Y_k$ for every $k$, i.e.\ in $\bigcap_k Y_k = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: A point in every D_n is constant, so its value lies in the empty intersection.

nodes.name: The cylinders are measurable
nodes.statement: Each $D_n$ is measurable.
conclusions: Each $D_n$ is measurable.
nodes.label: lem:diag-measurable

nodes.name: Proof of The cylinders are measurable
nodes.statement: Coordinate evaluation is measurable (\texttt{measurable\_coord}), hence so is agreement of two coordinates (\texttt{measurableSet\_eq\_coord}), and $D_n = \bigcap_{i \leq n} \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0\}$ is a finite intersection of those.
nodes.statement_short: Finite intersection of measurable coordinate-agreement sets.

nodes.name: Continuity from above, in the form the contradiction uses
nodes.statement: A probability measure cannot give every term of an antitone measurable sequence mass one when the intersection is empty.
conclusions: A probability measure cannot give every term of an antitone measurable sequence mass one when the intersection is empty.
nodes.label: lem:cont-above

nodes.name: Proof of Continuity from above, in the form the contradiction uses
nodes.statement: The measures converge to that of the intersection, which is $0$; if every term were $1$ the limit would be both $0$ and $1$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity from above forces the limit to be both 0 and 1.

nodes.name: Delay query
nodes.statement: Over a sensor alphabet $X$, the observation space is the bi-infinite stream space $\Omega = X^{\mathbb{Z}}$. The query at $(d,\tau)$ reads $d$ samples backwards at lag $\tau$: \[ \mathrm{eval}_{d,\tau}(\omega) = (\omega_0, \omega_{-\tau}, \omega_{-2\tau}, \dots, \omega_{-(d-1)\tau}) \in X^d . \]
nodes.statement_short: The (d,τ) query reads d samples of a bi-infinite stream backwards at lag τ.
nodes.label: def:delay-query

nodes.name: Delay refinement
nodes.statement: $(d,\tau) \leq (d',\tau')$ when $\tau' \mid \tau$ and $d' > (d-1)(\tau/\tau')$: the finer lag divides the coarser one, and the finer window is long enough to span the coarser one. The refinement map keeps the coordinates at positions $0, \tau/\tau', \dots, (d-1)\tau/\tau'$.
nodes.statement_short: (d,τ) ≤ (d',τ') when τ' divides τ and the finer window spans the coarser; refinement keeps matching coordinates.
nodes.label: def:delay-refine

nodes.name: The delay system is a query system
nodes.statement: $(d,\tau) \mapsto$ the delay query, with the refinement above, satisfies the query-system axioms.
conclusions: satisfies the query-system axioms
nodes.label: thm:delay-qs

nodes.name: Proof of The delay system is a query system
nodes.statement: Reflexivity and transitivity of the order are divisibility and arithmetic; $\pi_{\mathrm{refl}}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{trans}}$ are index computations on coordinate selections.
nodes.statement_short: Order axioms by divisibility arithmetic; refinement maps by index computations.

nodes.name: Delay system is upper-directed
nodes.statement: Any two delay queries have a common refinement.
conclusions: Any two delay queries have a common refinement.
nodes.label: thm:delay-upper

nodes.name: Proof of Upper-directed
nodes.statement: Take lag $\gcd(\tau,\tau')$ and depth $\max\{(d-1)(\tau/\gcd), (d'-1)(\tau'/\gcd)\} + 1$. The gcd divides both lags, and the depth is chosen to span both windows.
nodes.statement_short: Take lag gcd and a depth spanning both windows.

nodes.name: The delay system is NOT sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: There is no single query above the whole sequence $u_n = (n+2,\ 1)$.
conclusions: There is no single query above the whole sequence $u_n = (n+2,\ 1)$.
nodes.label: thm:delay-not-sud

nodes.name: Proof of The delay system is NOT sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: An upper bound $(d'',\tau'')$ would need $\tau'' \mid 1$, hence $\tau''=1$, and then $(n+2)-1 = n+1 < d''$ for every $n$ --- impossible for a finite $d''$.
nodes.statement_short: An upper bound would need lag 1 and unbounded depth.

nodes.name: Bounded fixed-lag subsystem
nodes.statement: Fix a lag $\tau_0$ and a maximum depth $N$; index by $\{d \leq N\}$ with the order $d \leq d'$ and coordinate-truncation refinement.

nodes.statement: $N$ is a universal upper bound.

conclusions: $N$ is a universal upper bound.

nodes.name: Proof of The bounded subsystem is sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: Every index is $\leq N$, so the constant family at $N$ bounds any sequence.

nodes.name: Extension for bounded fixed-lag delay embeddings
nodes.statement: For fixed $\tau_0$ and $N$, any compatible family of probability marginals on $\{X^d : d \leq N\}$ extends \emph{uniquely} to a probability measure on $\Omega$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Where the extension theorem does apply
conclusions: any compatible family of probability marginals on $\{X^d : d \leq N\}$ extends \emph{uniquely} to a probability measure on $\Omega$

nodes.name: Proof of Extension for bounded fixed-lag delay embeddings
nodes.statement: \ref{thm:delay-fixed-sud} supplies sequential upper-directedness and \texttt{evalSurjective} the realizability hypothesis; the extension theorem applies directly.
nodes.section: 4.3 Where the extension theorem does apply
nodes.statement_short: Supply sequential upper-directedness and surjectivity, then apply the extension theorem.

nodes.name: Conventions for the delay/reconstruction join
nodes.statement:
The join rests on two conventions. The query system's parameter is the
\textbf{observation} space: \ref{def:delay-query} samples streams
$\mathbb{Z} \to Y$, and the state space never appears in it. And
\ref{def:delay-query} samples the past, at $0, -\tau, \dots, -(d-1)\tau$, while
reconstruction iterates $T$ forward; the two agree once reading the stream
backwards is reading the orbit forwards. Reading past times as \emph{backward}
iterates instead would need $T$ invertible, and for invertible $T$ the two
generate the same $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.section: 4.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.statement_short: Observation-space parametrization and past sampling vs forward iteration agree; invertible T gives the same σ-algebra.

nodes.name: The delay map $\Phi_h$
nodes.statement: $\Phi_h(x) = (h(T^n x))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, the forward orbit of $x$ seen through the observable $h$. Paper II indexes on $\mathbb{Z}$; the Lean development indexes on $\mathbb{N}$, which for invertible $T$ generates the same $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.label: def:delay-map

nodes.name: The observable algebra $\mathcal{O}_h$
nodes.statement: The $\sigma$-algebra on the state space generated by a family $f : \mathbb{Z} \to (X \to \mathbb{R})$; $\mathcal{O}_h := \mathrm{observableAlgebra}(n \mapsto h \circ T^{n})$ (\texttt{delayObservableAlgebra}).
nodes.label: def:observable-algebra

nodes.name: Pullback identity
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{O}_h = \Phi_h^{-1}(\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}))$.
conclusions: $\mathcal{O}_h = \Phi_h^{-1}(\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}))$.
nodes.label: thm:obs-eq-comap

nodes.name: Proof of Pullback identity
nodes.statement: $(\le)$ each generator $h \circ T^{n}$ is $\pi_n \circ \Phi_h$, so its level sets are pullbacks. $(\ge)$ the product $\sigma$-algebra is generated by the coordinate projections, and $\Phi_h^{-1}(\pi_n^{-1}(E)) = (h \circ T^n)^{-1}(E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Two inclusions: generators are coordinates of Φ_h, and coordinate projections generate the product σ-algebra.

nodes.name: Density bridge, Paper II Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: The $m$-simple functions are dense in $L^2(X, m, \mu|_m)$.
conclusions: The $m$-simple functions are dense in $L^2(X, m, \mu|_m)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Density bridge, Paper II Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: \texttt{Lp.simpleFunc.dense}.

nodes.name: Reconstruction, Paper II Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{O}_h = m_0$ modulo $\mu$ if and only if $\mathrm{lpMeas}\,\mathcal{O}_h$ is dense in $L^2(\mu)$; and by \ref{thm:obs-eq-comap} both are equivalent to $\Phi_h$ being a measure-theoretic embedding.
conclusions: $\mathcal{O}_h = m_0$ modulo $\mu$ if and only if $\mathrm{lpMeas}\,\mathcal{O}_h$ is dense in $L^2(\mu)$
nodes.statement_short: The observable algebra is full mod μ iff its L² functions are dense, iff the delay map is a measure-theoretic embedding.
nodes.label: thm:reconstruction

nodes.name: Proof of Reconstruction, Paper II Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: Closed-plus-dense on the \texttt{lpMeas} subspace, with \ref{thm:density-bridge} supplying density.
nodes.statement_short: Closed-plus-dense argument on the lpMeas subspace, using the density bridge.

nodes.name: The observation stream of a state
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x$ is the sensor stream a state emits: at time $t$ it carries $h(T^{(-t)^{+}} x)$, the observation of the state $(-t)$ steps ahead.
nodes.label: def:orbit-stream

nodes.name: Sampling the orbit stream is taking delay coordinates
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{delayEval}\,d\,\tau\,(\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x) = (h(T^{k\tau} x))_{k < d}$. At $\tau = 1$ this is $\Phi_h$ truncated to its first $d$ coordinates (\texttt{delayEval\_orbitStream\_one}).
conclusions: $\mathrm{delayEval}\,d\,\tau\,(\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x) = (h(T^{k\tau} x))_{k < d}$
nodes.label: thm:delay-eval-orbit

nodes.name: Proof of Sampling the orbit stream is taking delay coordinates
nodes.statement: Unfold both sides; the time index $-(k\tau)$ negates to $k\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold both sides; negate the time index.

nodes.name: The bridge: the queries resolve exactly $\mathcal{O}_h$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra induced on the state space by pulling every delay query's outcome back along \ref{def:orbit-stream}. Then \[ \mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}\,h\,T = \mathcal{O}_h. \]
assumptions: Let $\mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra induced on the state space by pulling every delay query's outcome back along \ref{def:orbit-stream}.
conclusions: \[ \mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}\,h\,T = \mathcal{O}_h. \]
nodes.statement_short: The σ-algebra generated by all delay queries on the orbit stream equals the observable algebra O_h.
nodes.label: thm:query-reconstruction-bridge

nodes.name: Proof of The bridge: the queries resolve exactly $\mathcal{O}_h$
nodes.statement: $(\le)$ every coordinate of every query is some $h \circ T^{n}$ by \ref{thm:delay-eval-orbit}, so each query map is $\mathcal{O}_h$-measurable and its pullback sits below. $(\ge)$ conversely every generator $h \circ T^{n}$ is a coordinate of the query $(n+1, 1)$; the negative indices of the $\mathbb{Z}$-indexed family collapse to $h$ itself and are covered by $d = 1$. Unit lag alone therefore already generates everything.
nodes.statement_short: Two inclusions: query coordinates are generators of O_h, and each generator is a coordinate of a unit-lag query.

nodes.name: (≤): query coordinates are generators of O_h

nodes.name: The delay lag is the pruning ring length
nodes.statement:
\ref{thm:query-reconstruction-bridge} ranges over every lag, and unit lag alone
already attains the supremum, so $\tau$ is invisible to it. Fixing $\tau$ puts
it back. \ref{def:delay-query} samples at $0, -\tau, \dots, -(d-1)\tau$, while
\ref{def:lisc}'s layered ring $R_L$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_L \times A$ with
layer position mod $L$: the delay chapter's lag is the pruning chapter's ring
length.

nodes.name: Fixed lag resolves exactly the observable algebra of $T^{\tau}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{delayQueryAlgebraAtLag}\,h\,T\,\tau$ be the $\sigma$-algebra induced by the delay queries \emph{at the single lag} $\tau$. Then \[ \mathrm{delayQueryAlgebraAtLag}\,h\,T\,\tau = \mathcal{O}_h(T^{\tau}). \] In general $\mathcal{O}_h(T^{\tau}) < \mathcal{O}_h(T)$ strictly; at $\tau = 1$ nothing is lost (\texttt{delayQueryAlgebraAtLag\_one}).

nodes.name: Proof of Fixed lag resolves exactly the observable algebra of $T^{\tau}$
nodes.statement: Both inclusions as in \ref{thm:query-reconstruction-bridge}, with $T^{\tau}$ in place of $T$: every coordinate at lag $\tau$ is some $h \circ (T^{\tau})^n$ by \ref{thm:delay-eval-iterate}, and conversely each such generator is coordinate $n$ of the query $(n+1, \tau)$.

nodes.name: Intersection-closure
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{InterClosed}(d)$ says $A, A' \in d \Rightarrow A \cap A' \in d$. A Dynkin system with this property is exactly a $\sigma$-algebra, by Dynkin's $\pi$--$\lambda$ theorem.
nodes.label: def:interclosed

nodes.name: Distributivity is spent here, and only here
nodes.statement: On an intersection-closed carrier a two-valued state is \emph{multiplicative}: if $A$ and $A'$ are true, so is $A \cap A'$.

nodes.name: Proof of Distributivity is spent here, and only here
nodes.statement: $A = (A \cap A') \sqcup (A \cap A'^{c})$ is a disjoint union inside $d$. Since $A \cap A'^{c} \subseteq A'^{c}$ and $A'$ is true, monotonicity makes $A \cap A'^{c}$ false; additivity on the disjoint pair forces $A \cap A'$ true.
nodes.statement_short: Split A into A∩A' and A∩A'^c; monotonicity and additivity force A∩A' true.

nodes.name: Orthomodular lattice
nodes.statement: A bounded lattice with an order-reversing involution $x \mapsto x^{\perp}$ satisfying $x \wedge x^{\perp} = \bot$, $x \vee x^{\perp} = \top$, and the orthomodular law $x \le y \Rightarrow y = x \vee (y \wedge x^{\perp})$. Distributivity is not assumed; a distributive one is a Boolean algebra.
differentia: with an order-reversing involution $x \mapsto x^{\perp}$ satisfying $x \wedge x^{\perp} = \bot$, $x \vee x^{\perp} = \top$, and the orthomodular law $x \le y \Rightarrow y = x \vee (y \wedge x^{\perp})$
nodes.label: def:oml

nodes.name: MO$_2$
nodes.statement: The six-element lattice $\{\bot, a, a', b, b', \top\}$ with the four middle elements pairwise incomparable, $a^{\perp} = a'$ and $b^{\perp} = b'$.

nodes.name: The four-point carrier
nodes.statement: On $\Omega = \{0,1\}^{2}$ set $A = \{p : p_1 = 1\}$ and $B = \{p : p_2 = 1\}$, and let \[ L \;=\; \{\emptyset, A, A^{c}, \Omega\} \;\cup\; \{\emptyset, B, B^{c}, \Omega\}, \] the horizontal sum of two four-element Boolean blocks glued along $\{\emptyset, \Omega\}$. $L$ is a Dynkin system.
nodes.section: 5.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.statement_short: On {0,1}², L is the horizontal sum of the two Boolean blocks generated by A={p₁=1} and B={p₂=1}.

nodes.name: Proof that $L$ is a Dynkin system
nodes.statement: Complement-closure is immediate. For countable disjoint unions: two nonempty members of $L$ that are disjoint are complementary, because a member of one block always meets a member of the other --- $A \cap B$, $A \cap B^{c}$, $A^{c} \cap B$, $A^{c} \cap B^{c}$ are each a point. So a disjoint family in $L$ contains at most one nonempty member up to its complement, and its union is $\emptyset$, that member, or $\Omega$.

nodes.statement_short: Complements are immediate; disjoint nonempty members are complementary, so disjoint unions stay in L.

nodes.name: Concrete compatibility, and a poor pair
nodes.statement: $A \leftrightarrow B$ (\emph{compatible}) means $A \cap B$ is itself in the carrier. The pair is \emph{poor} when $A \cap B$ is inhabited and yet the only carrier member inside it is $\emptyset$: the lattice meet is $\bot$ while the intersection is not.

nodes.name: The four-point carrier has a poor pair
nodes.statement: $A \cap B$ is the single point $(1,1)$, which is not in $L$, and no nonempty member of $L$ fits inside it. So $(A,B)$ is poor, and $A$ and $B$ lie in no common maximal block.

nodes.statement: $A$ and $B$ lie in $L$ (\ref{thm:concrete-mo2-iso}), so intersection-closure would put $A \cap B$ in $L$ as well. By \ref{thm:concrete-mo2-poor} the only member of $L$ inside $A \cap B$ is $\emptyset$, and $A \cap B$ is inhabited.

nodes.name: Four points are necessary, and $L$ attains the bound
nodes.statement: If $S$ and $T$ lie in a $\sigma$-class and $S \cap T$ does not, then $S \cap T$, $S \setminus T$, $T \setminus S$ and $(S \cup T)^{c}$ are all inhabited, so the carrier has at least four points. Every $\sigma$-class on three or fewer points is therefore intersection-closed, hence a $\sigma$-algebra; and $|\Omega| = 4$, so $L$ realizes the failure on the smallest carrier that admits one.

nodes.name: Proof of Four points are necessary, and $L$ attains the bound
nodes.statement: Each cell is forced by a different closure property. $S \cap T = \emptyset$ would put it in the carrier. $S \setminus T = \emptyset$ gives $S \subseteq T$ and $S \cap T = S$; symmetrically $T \setminus S = \emptyset$ gives $S \cap T = T$. And $(S \cup T)^{c} = \emptyset$ makes $S^{c}$ and $T^{c}$ disjoint members, so $S^{c} \cup T^{c}$ lies in the carrier and its complement is $S \cap T$. The four cells are pairwise disjoint, so one point from each gives four distinct points.

nodes.statement_short: Each of the four cells is forced inhabited by a different closure property; one point per cell.

nodes.statement: A Dynkin system. Complement and countable disjoint union are computed fibrewise --- the fibre of a complement is the complement of the fibre, the fibre of a union the union of the fibres, and disjointness passes to fibres --- so each closure property reduces to the same property of \ref{def:concrete-mo2}.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-class = concrete $\sigma$-complete OMP
nodes.statement: A family $L \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ with $\emptyset, \Omega \in L$, closed under complement, and closed under countable \emph{disjoint} unions. Formalized as Mathlib's \texttt{DynkinSystem}: \texttt{has\_iUnion\_nat} takes \texttt{Pairwise (Disjoint on f)}, so this is a $\sigma$-class and not a $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.label: def:sigma-class

nodes.name: $\sigma$-additive two-valued state
nodes.statement: $s : L \to \{0,1\}$ with $s(\Omega) = 1$, additive over countable orthogonal joins. The paper's $s(\bigcup_n A_n) = \sum_n s(A_n)$ becomes ``union true if and only if some member true''; the at-most-one half is derived (\texttt{val\_at\_most\_one}) rather than assumed.
nodes.label: def:two-valued-state

nodes.name: Finitely additive two-valued state
nodes.statement: Pair additivity only. Finite-family additivity is derived (\texttt{val\_sUnion\_finset}).
nodes.label: def:finadd-state

nodes.name: The local pattern
nodes.statement: A two-valued assignment on a finite $\perp$-closed block $B \subseteq L$. \texttt{LocalState} demands only complement-additivity inside $B$, which is weaker in general than the paper's Def 1.2 restricted to $B$.
nodes.label: def:local-pattern

nodes.name: The weaker encoding is upgraded by coherence
nodes.statement: A finitely coherent \texttt{LocalState} satisfies every Def-1.2 constraint on $B$.
conclusions: satisfies every Def-1.2 constraint on $B$
nodes.label: lem:pattern-fully-additive

nodes.name: Proof of The weaker encoding is upgraded by coherence
nodes.statement: Coherence supplies a finitely additive extension on all of $L$; its additivity restricts to every Def-1.2 constraint on the finite block $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the finitely additive extension supplied by coherence to the block.

nodes.name: On the witness block the encodings coincide outright
nodes.statement: On the witness's own block the only disjoint pairs are the complement pairs, so there \texttt{LocalState} equals Def 1.2-on-$B$ exactly, coherence or not.
conclusions: On the witness's own block the only disjoint pairs are the complement pairs
nodes.label: lem:coreblock-disjoint

nodes.name: Proof of On the witness block the encodings coincide outright
nodes.statement: The twelve cross-intersections of the three cores and their complements are each exhibited nonempty, so the only disjoint pairs are the complement pairs.
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit the twelve cross-intersections nonempty.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-essential contextual state
nodes.statement: $s_0$ is finitely coherent (extends to \emph{some} finitely additive two-valued state on all of $L$) and extends to \textbf{no} global $\sigma$-additive two-valued state. Extension means agreement on $B$.
nodes.label: def:sigma-essential

nodes.name: $\Psi$: the localized existence sentence
nodes.statement: Some $\Omega$, $\sigma$-class, block and pattern with $s_0$ $\sigma$-essential. Admissibility predicates are not bundled in: non-Booleanness is \ref{lem:carrier-not-boolean}.
nodes.label: def:psi

nodes.name: Localization --- the whole content is clause (ii)
nodes.statement: $s_0$ is a witness if and only if (0) it is finitely coherent, (i) no point-evaluation extends it ($K(s_0) = \emptyset$), \emph{and} (ii) no non-Dirac $\sigma$-additive two-valued state does. Clause (i) is freely arrangeable by the Navara--Pt\'ak intersection device.
equivalent_conditions: (0) it is finitely coherent, (i) no point-evaluation extends it ($K(s_0) = \emptyset$), \emph{and} (ii) no non-Dirac $\sigma$-additive two-valued state does
conclusions: $s_0$ is a witness if and only if (0) it is finitely coherent, (i) no point-evaluation extends it ($K(s_0) = \emptyset$), \emph{and} (ii) no non-Dirac $\sigma$-additive two-valued state does
nodes.statement_short: A pattern is a σ-essential witness iff coherent, with empty kernel, and with no non-Dirac σ-additive extension.
nodes.label: thm:localization

nodes.name: Proof of Localization --- the whole content is clause (ii)
nodes.statement: A global $\sigma$-additive two-valued state either agrees with a point evaluation on the carrier or does not; splitting on that alternative gives clauses (i) and (ii). Clause (0) is the coherence conjunct, carried through unchanged.
nodes.statement_short: Split on whether a σ-state agrees with a point evaluation.

nodes.name: No witness on a Boolean carrier
nodes.statement: On an intersection-closed (Boolean) carrier no $\sigma$-essential contextual state exists (Prop 2.1).
conclusions: no $\sigma$-essential contextual state exists
nodes.label: lem:boolean-no-witness

nodes.name: Proof of No witness on a Boolean carrier
nodes.statement: Via \texttt{boolean\_baseline}: the finitely additive extension supplied by coherence is multiplicative on the intersection-closed carrier, so the block's true sets have the finite intersection property; a common point is a kernel point.
nodes.statement_short: Boolean baseline: multiplicative extension gives the finite intersection property and a kernel point.

nodes.name: $\Omega_7$: a Boolean pattern that fails only coherence
nodes.statement: $\Omega_7$ is the seven-point Boolean carrier $\{+,-\}^3 \setminus \{(+,+,+)\}$, and $s_0$ the majority vote of the three marked points. Then $s_0$ has empty kernel and no $\sigma$-additive two-valued extension, and $s_0$ is not finitely coherent. So $s_0$ satisfies every clause of \ref{def:sigma-essential} except coherence, and is not a witness.
assumptions: $\Omega_7$ is the seven-point Boolean carrier $\{+,-\}^3 \setminus \{(+,+,+)\}$, and $s_0$ the majority vote of the three marked points.
conclusions: $s_0$ has empty kernel and no $\sigma$-additive two-valued extension, and $s_0$ is not finitely coherent
nodes.label: thm:omega7

nodes.name: Proof of $\Omega_7$: a Boolean pattern that fails only coherence
nodes.statement: The three coordinate events pairwise intersect and have empty triple intersection, so no point realises $s_0$ and no $\sigma$-additive state extends it (\texttt{omega7\_no\_sigma\_extension}). The carrier is Boolean, so by \ref{lem:boolean-no-witness} no pattern on it is a witness; the clause that fails is therefore coherence (\texttt{omega7\_not\_coherent}), and $s_0$ is not a witness (\texttt{omega7\_not\_witness}).
nodes.statement_short: Pairwise-intersecting coordinate events with empty triple intersection; Booleanness then forces coherence to fail.

nodes.name: Ulam matrix
nodes.statement: Rows disjoint, rows covering above the index, columns exactly disjoint.
nodes.label: def:ulam-matrix

nodes.name: Carrier, block, pattern
nodes.statement: $\Omega = \omega_1 \times \{1,2,3,4\}$ with cores $A_1 = M\times\{1,2\}$, $A_2 = M\times\{1,3\}$, $A_3 = M\times\{2,3\}$; $L$ the least $\sigma$-class containing singletons, cells and cores; $B$ the $\perp$-closure of the cores; $s_0 \equiv 1$ on the three cores, encoded as the majority vote of three marked points (self-dual, so the complement values are forced).
nodes.statement_short: Carrier on ω₁×{1,2,3,4}: the least σ-class with singletons, cells and three cores; block B and the all-true core pattern s₀.
nodes.label: def:core-block

nodes.name: The $\omega_1$ instantiation
nodes.statement: $M_1 = \omega_1$ as a type: uncountable, with every initial segment countable.
conclusions: uncountable, with every initial segment countable
nodes.label: lem:omega1

nodes.name: Proof of The $\omega_1$ instantiation
nodes.statement: From Mathlib's ordinal API: cardinality $\aleph_1$ gives uncountability, and $\mathrm{typein} < \omega_1$ gives countability of every initial segment.
nodes.statement_short: Mathlib's ordinal API.

nodes.name: Rigidity --- every $\sigma$-state is Dirac on the carrier
nodes.statement: For any uncountable $M$ with countable initial segments carrying an Ulam matrix, every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state on the carrier agrees with some $\delta_\omega$ on it (\texttt{IsDiracOn}).
assumptions: For any uncountable $M$ with countable initial segments carrying an Ulam matrix
conclusions: every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state on the carrier agrees with some $\delta_\omega$ on it
nodes.label: thm:rigidity

nodes.name: Proof of Rigidity --- every $\sigma$-state is Dirac on the carrier
nodes.statement: Exact column disjointness forces all but countably many columns to miss the support of a $\sigma$-additive two-valued state; row covering above the index then pins the support to a single point.
nodes.statement_short: Column disjointness leaves countably many columns; row covering pins the support to a point.

nodes.name: The carrier is not Boolean
nodes.statement: $L_1$ is not intersection-closed.
conclusions: $L_1$ is not intersection-closed.
nodes.label: lem:carrier-not-boolean

nodes.name: Proof of The carrier is not Boolean
nodes.statement: A Boolean carrier admits no witness (\ref{lem:boolean-no-witness}), and the pattern is a witness (\ref{thm:core-pattern-witness} at $\omega_1$).
nodes.statement_short: A Boolean carrier has no witness, but this one does.

nodes.name: $\Psi$, in ZFC
nodes.statement: $\Psi$ holds on $\sigma$-classes/OMPs, irreducible modulo the countable ideal, in ZFC.
conclusions: $\Psi$ holds on $\sigma$-classes/OMPs, irreducible modulo the countable ideal, in ZFC.
nodes.label: thm:psi-zfc

nodes.name: Proof of $\Psi$, in ZFC
nodes.statement: \ref{thm:core-pattern-witness} assembled at $\omega_1$ via \ref{lem:omega1}.
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the witness at ω₁.

nodes.name: Thm 3.5 --- normal form for carrier sets
nodes.statement: Every set in the carrier has a normalized representation, with coordinate $3$ as the anchor.
conclusions: Every set in the carrier has a normalized representation, with coordinate $3$ as the anchor.
nodes.label: thm:normal-form

nodes.name: Proof of Thm 3.5 --- normal form for carrier sets
nodes.statement: By \texttt{GenerateHas} induction. The disjointness table supplies all four cases, including the parity-triangle impossibility, and the trichotomy is inline.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on GenerateHas with the disjointness table.

nodes.name: $\S$6 --- the vote state, and coherence
nodes.statement: The majority-vote assignment is a finitely additive two-valued state on the whole carrier, and it extends the core pattern.
conclusions: The majority-vote assignment is a finitely additive two-valued state on the whole carrier
it extends the core pattern
nodes.label: thm:vote-state

nodes.name: Proof of $\S$6 --- the vote state, and coherence
nodes.statement: \texttt{mVal} is well defined by representation rigidity (3.2); additivity is read off the disjointness table (3.3); agreement with the pattern on the three cores is Cor 6.4.
nodes.statement_short: Well-definedness by representation rigidity, additivity from the disjointness table.

nodes.name: The witness, assembled
nodes.statement: Coherence (\ref{thm:vote-state}) together with rigidity (\ref{thm:rigidity}) gives a pattern that is finitely coherent and has no global $\sigma$-additive extension --- a $\sigma$-essential contextual state.
conclusions: gives a pattern that is finitely coherent and has no global $\sigma$-additive extension
nodes.label: thm:core-pattern-witness

nodes.name: Proof of The witness, assembled
nodes.statement: Coherence gives the positive clause, rigidity the negative one.
nodes.statement_short: Coherence gives the positive clause, rigidity the negative.

nodes.name: The carrier is not Polish-representable
nodes.statement: Write $\mathrm{DWPolishCut}$ for the statement that a Polish-representable carrier admits no $\sigma$-essential witness. Granting it, $L_1$ is not Polish-representable. The hypothesis is carried explicitly.
nodes.section: 6.4 The OML gap --- the open question
conclusions: $L_1$ is not Polish-representable
nodes.label: lem:carrier-not-polish

nodes.name: Proof of The carrier is not Polish-representable
nodes.statement: $L_1$ carries a witness (\ref{thm:psi-zfc}), and the cut forbids a witness on a Polish-representable carrier.
nodes.section: 6.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.statement_short: L₁ carries a witness, which the cut forbids on Polish carriers.

nodes.name: The Polish cut is clause (i), not extra leverage
nodes.statement: Granting that Polish-representability forces every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state to be a point evaluation, the cut of \ref{lem:carrier-not-polish} is equivalent to clause (i) restricted to Polish carriers: every finitely coherent pattern there has a nonempty kernel.
nodes.section: 6.4 The OML gap --- the open question
assumptions: Granting that Polish-representability forces every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state to be a point evaluation
conclusions: the cut of \ref{lem:carrier-not-polish} is equivalent to clause (i) restricted to Polish carriers
nodes.label: thm:polish-cut-reduced

nodes.name: Proof of The Polish cut is clause (i), not extra leverage
nodes.statement: \ref{thm:localization} splits a witness into (0) coherence, (i) empty kernel and (ii) no non-Dirac $\sigma$-state extending. If every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state is a point evaluation then clause (ii) holds vacuously, so being a witness is exactly (0) $\wedge$ (i), and "no witness" is exactly "coherent $\Rightarrow$ kernel nonempty".
nodes.section: 6.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.statement_short: Localization with clause (ii) vacuous reduces no-witness to coherent implies nonempty kernel.

nodes.name: Finite additivity is $\sigma$-additivity on a finite carrier
nodes.statement: On a finite $\Omega$ every finitely additive state satisfies the $\sigma$-condition on the whole carrier.
conclusions: every finitely additive state satisfies the $\sigma$-condition on the whole carrier
nodes.label: lem:finite-sigma

nodes.name: Proof of Finite additivity is $\sigma$-additivity on a finite carrier
nodes.statement: A pairwise disjoint family in a finite space has only finitely many nonempty members --- choosing a point from each is injective --- so the countable union is the finite sup over that index set, and finite additivity applies to it.
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint families in a finite space have finitely many nonempty members; apply finite additivity.

nodes.name: $\Phi$ on finite carriers
nodes.statement: No finite $\sigma$-class admits a $\sigma$-essential witness; equivalently, a witness carrier is infinite. The finite and Boolean gates are independent: the four-point carrier of \ref{def:concrete-mo2} is finite and not intersection-closed.
conclusions: No finite $\sigma$-class admits a $\sigma$-essential witness; equivalently, a witness carrier is infinite.
nodes.label: thm:phi-finite

nodes.name: Proof of $\Phi$ on finite carriers
nodes.statement: Coherence supplies a finitely additive state extending the pattern; \ref{lem:finite-sigma} makes it $\sigma$-additive, so it is a global $\sigma$-additive two-valued state extending the pattern and the pattern is not $\sigma$-essential.
nodes.statement_short: Coherent extension is σ-additive on a finite carrier, so the pattern is not σ-essential.

nodes.name: One block iff Boolean
nodes.statement: A carrier has a unique maximal block if and only if it is intersection-closed. Hence $\Phi$ holds on one-block carriers.
equivalent_conditions: A carrier has a unique maximal block
conclusions: A carrier has a unique maximal block if and only if it is intersection-closed.
Hence $\Phi$ holds on one-block carriers.
nodes.label: thm:one-block-iff-boolean

nodes.name: Proof of One block iff Boolean
nodes.statement: If every pair is compatible the whole carrier is a compatible family, and maximality forces each maximal block to be all of it. Conversely each singleton $\{A\}$ extends to a maximal block, uniqueness puts $A$ and $B$ in the same one, and members of a block are compatible. The $\Phi$ half is then \ref{lem:boolean-no-witness}.
nodes.statement_short: Both directions via compatibility and maximal blocks; the Φ half by the Boolean no-witness lemma.

nodes.name: Compatible carrier gives one maximal block
nodes.statement:
If every pair is compatible the whole carrier is a compatible family, and
  maximality forces each maximal block to be all of it.
nodes.statement_short: Compatible carrier gives one maximal block

nodes.name: Unique maximal block gives compatibility
nodes.statement:
Conversely each
  singleton $\{A\}$ extends to a maximal block, uniqueness puts $A$ and $B$ in
  the same one, and members of a block are compatible.
nodes.statement_short: Unique maximal block gives compatibility

nodes.name: Φ half by the Boolean no-witness lemma
nodes.statement:
The $\Phi$ half is then
  \ref{lem:boolean-no-witness}.
nodes.statement_short: Φ half by the Boolean no-witness lemma

nodes.name: Concentration on a countable partition
nodes.statement: If the carrier contains a countable partition of $\Omega$, every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state is true on exactly one part.
assumptions: the carrier contains a countable partition of $\Omega$
conclusions: every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state is true on exactly one part
nodes.label: lem:concentration-partition

nodes.name: Proof of Concentration on a countable partition
nodes.statement: Existence is $\sigma$-additivity applied to the partition, whose union is $\Omega$; uniqueness is two-valuedness on a disjoint pair.
nodes.statement_short: σ-additivity on the partition for existence, two-valuedness for uniqueness.

nodes.name: Countable carriers with singletons are point-determined
nodes.statement: If $\Omega$ is countable and every singleton lies in the carrier, then every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state agrees on the carrier with a point evaluation. Consequently a pattern there is a witness exactly when it is finitely coherent with empty kernel: clause (ii) of \ref{thm:localization} is vacuous, and the whole question is clause (i).
assumptions: $\Omega$ is countable and every singleton lies in the carrier
conclusions: every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state agrees on the carrier with a point evaluation
a pattern there is a witness exactly when it is finitely coherent with empty kernel
nodes.label: thm:countable-point-determined

nodes.name: Proof of Countable carriers with singletons are point-determined
nodes.statement: The singletons partition $\Omega$ into a countable pairwise disjoint family inside the carrier, so $\sigma$-additivity places the state's mass on one of them, at $\omega$ say; monotonicity and complement-additivity then give $s(A) = 1 \iff \omega \in A$ for every carrier set. For the consequence: any $\sigma$-additive state extending the pattern agrees with $\delta_\omega$ on the block, so $\delta_\omega$ extends it too and $\omega$ lies in the kernel.
nodes.statement_short: Singletons partition Ω, so σ-additivity concentrates the state at a point.

nodes.name: The witness carrier is not a lattice
nodes.statement: $L_1$ has no meet at the cores: a greatest lower bound would have to be the slab $M \times \{0\}$, which is not in the carrier.
conclusions: $L_1$ has no meet at the cores
nodes.label: lem:witness-not-lattice

nodes.name: Proof of The witness carrier is not a lattice
nodes.statement: Forced by the singletons, a greatest carrier lower bound of the cores would have to equal the slab $M \times \{0\}$ (\texttt{greatest\_lowerBound\_eq\_slab}). The slab is not in the carrier (\texttt{slab0\_not\_mem}): any normalized representation must give coordinate $0$ a code differing from the other three (\texttt{slab\_codes\_differ}, since the $f = 0$ trace is co-countable and the rest are countable), so the code is the odd-weight $1000$ or its complement $0111$, and \texttt{EvenCode} excludes both.
nodes.statement_short: A greatest lower bound of the cores would be the slab, which normal-form codes exclude.

nodes.name: $L_1$ is not order-isomorphic to any $\sigma$-algebra
nodes.statement: There is no order isomorphism between the carrier of $L_1$ and the measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra, on any space.
conclusions: There is no order isomorphism between the carrier of $L_1$ and the measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra, on any space.
nodes.label: cor:carrier-not-orderiso

nodes.name: Proof of $L_1$ is not order-isomorphic to any $\sigma$-algebra
nodes.statement: \texttt{MeetsExist} is a property of the carrier poset, so an order isomorphism transports it. The measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra are closed under intersection, so any two have a greatest measurable set below both; carrying that back along the isomorphism gives a greatest carrier element below any two carrier elements. \ref{lem:witness-not-lattice} says there is none below the two cores.
nodes.statement_short: Meets exist in σ-algebras and transfer along order isomorphisms, but fail at the cores.

nodes.name: MeetsExist transported by order isomorphisms
nodes.statement:
\texttt{MeetsExist} is a property of the carrier poset, so an order
  isomorphism transports it.
nodes.statement_short: MeetsExist transported by order isomorphisms

nodes.name: σ-algebras have meets, transported back
nodes.statement:
The measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra are
  closed under intersection, so any two have a greatest measurable set below
  both; carrying that back along the isomorphism gives a greatest carrier
  element below any two carrier elements.
nodes.statement_short: σ-algebras have meets, transported back

nodes.name: Contradiction at the cores
nodes.statement:
\ref{lem:witness-not-lattice} says
  there is none below the two cores.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction at the cores

nodes.name: Central set
nodes.statement: $E$ lies in the carrier and $E \cap A$ is again in the carrier for every carrier element $A$.
also_stated_at: A carrier element is \emph{central} when it meets every carrier element back inside the carrier.
nodes.label: def:central

nodes.name: All four traces of a central set agree
nodes.statement: A central $E$ has a single $\xi$ with $\mathrm{trace}(E,f) \approx \xi$ for every coordinate $f$.
conclusions: has a single $\xi$ with $\mathrm{trace}(E,f) \approx \xi$ for every coordinate $f$
nodes.label: thm:central-traces

nodes.name: Proof of All four traces of a central set agree
nodes.statement: Coordinates $0,1,2$ carry countably equal traces, $\kappa_3$ is false, and even weight forces the fourth. Equal traces force equal codes, since $\kappa_a \neq \kappa_b$ would make $\xi \approx \xi^{c}$ and $M$ countable.
nodes.statement_short: Countably equal traces at three coordinates and even weight force the fourth.

nodes.name: $\xi$-triviality, the paper's ${[E]} \in \{0,1\}$
nodes.statement: That common $\xi$ is countable or co-countable.
conclusions: That common $\xi$ is countable or co-countable.
nodes.label: thm:xi-trivial

nodes.name: Proof of $\xi$-triviality, the paper's ${[E]} \in \{0,1\}$
nodes.statement: Apply centrality at a core. $E \cap \mathrm{coreA}$ is again a carrier element, so \ref{thm:normal-form} represents it as $\eta^{(\kappa)}$ with $\kappa_3$ false. Meeting $\mathrm{coreA}$ empties coordinate $3$, where the normal form is anchored: $\emptyset \approx \eta$, so $\eta$ is countable. Coordinate $0$ is untouched by the meet and carries $\xi$, so $\xi \approx \eta$ or $\xi \approx \eta^{c}$ --- countable or co-countable respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Apply centrality at a core and use the normal form anchored at coordinate 3.

nodes.name: Centrality at coreA
nodes.statement:
Apply centrality at a core. $E \cap \mathrm{coreA}$ is again a carrier element,
so \ref{thm:normal-form} represents it as $\eta^{(\kappa)}$ with $\kappa_3$
false.
nodes.statement_short: Centrality at coreA; normal form of E∩coreA

nodes.name: η countable
nodes.statement:
Meeting $\mathrm{coreA}$ empties coordinate $3$, where the normal form is
anchored: $\emptyset \approx \eta$, so $\eta$ is countable.
nodes.statement_short: η countable

nodes.name: ξ countable or co-countable
nodes.statement:
Coordinate $0$ is
untouched by the meet and carries $\xi$, so $\xi \approx \eta$ or
$\xi \approx \eta^{c}$ --- countable or co-countable respectively.
nodes.statement_short: ξ countable or co-countable

nodes.name: The centre is trivial modulo the countable ideal
nodes.statement: A central set is countable or co-countable.
conclusions: A central set is countable or co-countable.
nodes.label: cor:centre

nodes.name: Proof of The centre is trivial modulo the countable ideal
nodes.statement: \ref{thm:central-traces} reduces the question to $\xi$ and \ref{thm:xi-trivial} makes $\xi$ trivial; countable traces force a countable set and co-countable traces a co-countable one.
nodes.statement_short: Traces reduce to ξ, which is trivial.

nodes.name: Segregated carrier, and non-segregation
nodes.statement: A carrier is \emph{segregated} when every finitely additive state is blockwise pointed --- each maximal block supplies a kernel point. \emph{Non-segregated} is the negation.
nodes.label: def:segregated

nodes.name: Non-segregation is forced by the witness
nodes.statement: A witness carrier is non-segregated.
conclusions: A witness carrier is non-segregated.
nodes.label: lem:witness-nonsegregated

nodes.name: Proof of Non-segregation is forced by the witness
nodes.statement: On a segregated carrier blockwise $\sigma$-additivity globalises, so every finitely additive state is $\sigma$-additive; a finitely coherent pattern then has a $\sigma$-additive realization and is not $\sigma$-essential.
nodes.statement_short: On a segregated carrier finitely additive states are σ-additive, so no σ-essential pattern.

nodes.name: The centre, and essential irreducibility
nodes.statement: $E$ is \emph{central} when it lies in the carrier and $E \cap A$ does too for every carrier element $A$. The carrier is \emph{essentially irreducible} when every central element is countable or co-countable.
nodes.label: def:essentially-irreducible

nodes.name: The admissible carrier class
nodes.statement: Essentially irreducible and non-segregated.
nodes.label: def:admissible

nodes.name: The witness carrier is admissible
nodes.statement: $L_1$ is essentially irreducible and non-segregated. So the sharp Exit-A target --- a witness on an admissible carrier --- is inhabited in ZFC by the $\omega_1$ product-Ulam witness.
conclusions: $L_1$ is essentially irreducible and non-segregated.
nodes.label: thm:l1-admissible

nodes.name: Proof of The witness carrier is admissible
nodes.statement: Essential irreducibility is \ref{cor:centre}: every central element of $L_1$ is countable or co-countable. Non-segregation is \ref{lem:witness-nonsegregated} applied to the witness of \ref{thm:psi-zfc}.
nodes.statement_short: Essential irreducibility from the trivial centre; non-segregation from the witness.

nodes.name: Irreducibility proper
nodes.statement: The centre is trivial: every central element is $\emptyset$ or $\Omega$. Strictly stronger than \ref{def:essentially-irreducible}.
nodes.label: def:irreducible

nodes.name: The concrete descent carrier is reducible
nodes.statement: Every block of \ref{def:concrete-descent} is central, so the centre has one element per subset of $\mathbb{N}$ and the carrier is not irreducible. It satisfies \ref{def:essentially-irreducible} vacuously, the carrier being countable; $L_1$'s carrier is uncountable, so there the dichotomy is real.
conclusions: the carrier is not irreducible
nodes.label: thm:descent-not-irreducible

nodes.name: Proof of The concrete descent carrier is reducible
nodes.statement: Meeting a carrier element with a whole block leaves each fibre either that fibre or empty, both in the four-point carrier, so blocks are central. Block $0$ is neither empty nor everything. Vacuity of the essential form is countability of $\mathbb{N} \times \{0,1\}^{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Blocks are central and nontrivial; essential irreducibility vacuous by countability.

nodes.name: Blocks are central
nodes.statement:
Meeting a carrier element with a whole block leaves each fibre either that
  fibre or empty, both in the four-point carrier, so blocks are central.
nodes.statement_short: Blocks are central

nodes.name: Block 0 is a nontrivial central element
nodes.statement:
Block
  $0$ is neither empty nor everything.
nodes.statement_short: Block 0 is a nontrivial central element

nodes.name: Countability gives vacuity
nodes.statement:
Vacuity of the essential form is
  countability of $\mathbb{N} \times \{0,1\}^{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Countability gives vacuity

nodes.name: $\Psi_{\mathrm{OML}}$ --- the lattice form
nodes.statement: The same existence sentence with latticehood (\texttt{MeetsExist}) adjoined to the carrier.
nodes.label: def:psi-oml

nodes.name: $\Phi$
nodes.statement: $\Phi$: does every concrete, $\sigma$-complete, non-Boolean, essentially irreducible OML have each finite trace of each finitely additive two-valued state reproduced by some $\sigma$-additive one? A positive answer is the negation of $\Psi_{\mathrm{OML}}$. Open.
nodes.statement_short: Open: does every concrete σ-complete non-Boolean essentially irreducible OML reproduce finite traces of finitely additive two-valued states σ-additively?
nodes.label: rmk:phi-open

nodes.name: Countably compact class
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{K}$ of sets such that every sequence from $\mathcal{K}$ with the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection.
nodes.section: 6.5.1 Transport: a compact class forces the $\sigma$-condition
nodes.label: def:countably-compact-class

nodes.name: Marczewski approximation, two-valued in-block form
nodes.statement: Every value-$1$ member $E$ of the family carries a value-$1$ inner witness sandwiched below a class member: $D \subseteq K \subseteq E$ with $K \in \mathcal{K}$.
nodes.section: 6.5.1 Transport: a compact class forces the $\sigma$-condition
nodes.label: def:approximates-on

nodes.name: Compact transport
nodes.statement: On a carrier where meets exist, a finitely additive two-valued state approximated on every maximal block by a countably compact class satisfies the $\sigma$-condition on the whole carrier.

nodes.name: Proof of Compact transport
nodes.statement: Run inside one maximal block and glue. Tails of a disjoint sequence are value-$1$, so their inner witnesses have value-$1$ --- hence nonempty --- finite intersections; the sandwiching compacts therefore have the finite intersection property, and countable compactness contradicts the empty tail intersection. Marczewski 1953, 4(i), two-valued.

nodes.name: Theorem-let R: (8.1) forces Dirac
nodes.statement: On a Hausdorff space, a two-valued finitely additive state satisfying (8.1) has nonempty $\mathcal{K}_1$ (its value-$1$ in-field compacts), nonempty $D = \bigcap \mathcal{K}_1$, and \emph{equals} $\delta_\omega$ on the field for every $\omega \in D$.

nodes.statement: Value-$1$ in-field compacts are $\cap$-stable (compact $\cap$ closed, and Hausdorff makes compacts closed), finite intersections are value-$1$ hence nonempty, and compactness of one fixed member turns an empty total intersection into an empty finite one.

nodes.name: Relation $\rho$ on alphabet $A$
nodes.statement:
Throughout, $\rho \subseteq A \times A$ is an arbitrary relation on an
arbitrary alphabet; finiteness of $A$ is assumed only where stated, and no
strong-connectivity hypothesis is used anywhere.
nodes.section: 7 The pruning theorem and eventual periodicity of Safe

nodes.name: Layer-injective simple cycle
nodes.statement: For $L \geq 1$ the \emph{layered ring} $R_L(\rho)$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_L \times A$ and arcs $(i,a) \to (i+1 \bmod L, b)$ for every $(a,b) \in \rho$. A simple cycle of \emph{winding} $k$ is a closed walk of length $kL$ with all vertices distinct. $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ holds when one exists. Encoded by the state sequence $W$ on positions $t < kL$: $\rho$-steps between consecutive positions, a closing $\rho$-step, and the simplicity clause --- same layer $(t \bmod L)$ plus same state implies same position.
nodes.section: 7.1 The two sides: cycles in the layered ring, walks in the tuple digraph
nodes.statement_short: Layered ring Z_L×A with ρ-arcs between consecutive layers; LISC_k(L) says a simple cycle of winding k exists.
nodes.label: def:lisc

nodes.name: Tuple digraph and rotation walks
nodes.statement: $T_k(\rho)$ has as vertices the \emph{injective} $k$-tuples $u \in A^k$, with arcs $u \to v$ iff $(u_j, v_j) \in \rho$ for every $j$. For $r \in \mathbb{Z}_k$ let $\sigma_r(u)_j = u_{j+r}$. Then $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ holds when some length-$L$ walk in $T_k(\rho)$ runs from a $u$ to $\sigma_r(u)$. Encoded as $\tau : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}_k \to A$ with $\tau_i$ injective for $i \leq L$, coordinatewise $\rho$-arcs, and endpoint $\tau_L\,j = \tau_0\,(j+r)$.
nodes.section: 7.1 The two sides: cycles in the layered ring, walks in the tuple digraph
nodes.statement_short: Digraph on injective k-tuples with coordinatewise ρ-arcs; TR_k^(r)(L) says a length-L walk goes from u to its rotation σ_r(u).
nodes.label: def:tr

nodes.name: Step 2: extraction
nodes.statement: For $0 < L$, $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ implies $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$.
conclusions: $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$
nodes.label: lem:extraction

nodes.name: Proof of Step 2: extraction
nodes.statement: Read the $k$ strands at each layer: set $\tau_i[j]$ to the state of $W[jL+i]$. Injectivity of each $\tau_i$ is forced by simplicity: distinct vertices at the same layer have distinct states. The endpoint computes to $\sigma_1(\tau_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Read the k strands at each layer; simplicity forces injectivity.

nodes.name: Define τ_i from the cycle strands
nodes.statement: Read the $k$ strands at each layer: set $\tau_i[j]$ to the state of $W[jL+i]$.
nodes.statement_short: Define τ_i from the cycle strands

nodes.name: Injectivity from simplicity
nodes.statement:
Injectivity of each $\tau_i$ is forced by simplicity: distinct vertices at the

nodes.name: Endpoint is the rotation
nodes.statement: The endpoint computes to $\sigma_1(\tau_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Endpoint is the rotation

nodes.name: Step 3: assembly
nodes.statement: For $0 < L$, $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ implies $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$.
conclusions: implies $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$
nodes.label: lem:assembly

nodes.name: Proof of Step 3: assembly
nodes.statement: Place position $t = jL+i$ at vertex $(i, \tau_i[j])$. Arcs within a strand are the tuple-walk arcs; at a strand boundary the rotation endpoint supplies $\tau_L[j] = \tau_0[j+1]$, which is the state at position $(j+1)L$, and at $j = k-1$ this is the closure. Simplicity follows from the layer clock plus injectivity of each $\tau_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Place positions on layered vertices; arcs from the walk, closure from the rotation endpoint.

nodes.name: Place positions on the layered ring
nodes.statement: Place position $t = jL+i$ at vertex $(i, \tau_i[j])$.

Arcs within a strand are
