nodes.name: Step 4: generator conjugation
nodes.statement: If $r$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_k$, that is $\gcd(r,k)=1$, then $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ does.
assumptions: $r$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_k$, that is $\gcd(r,k)=1$
conclusions: $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ does
nodes.label: lem:conjugation

nodes.name: Proof of Step 4: generator conjugation
nodes.statement: The slot relabelling $P(u)[j] = u[j\bar r]$, with $\bar r = r^{-1}$, is a bijection of injective tuples, preserves arcs (a fixed coordinate permutation), and conjugates the rotations via $(j+r)\bar r = j\bar r + 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Slot relabelling by r⁻¹ conjugates rotation r to rotation 1.

nodes.name: Theorem P
nodes.statement: For every $\rho$, every $L \geq 1$, every $k \geq 1$ and every $r$ generating $\mathbb{Z}_k$, $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ does.
assumptions: every $\rho$, every $L \geq 1$, every $k \geq 1$ and every $r$ generating $\mathbb{Z}_k$
conclusions: $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ does
nodes.statement_short: A layer-injective simple cycle of winding k exists iff a rotation-r walk in the tuple digraph does, for any generator r.
nodes.label: thm:pruning

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem P: pruning, phase-parametrized
nodes.statement: Conjugate to $r=1$ by \ref{lem:conjugation}, then combine \ref{lem:extraction} and \ref{lem:assembly}.
nodes.statement_short: Conjugate to r=1, then combine extraction and assembly.

nodes.name: Lemma NG: assembly half
nodes.statement: Suppose the rotation $r$ closes an orbit of size $m$, witnessed by an injective slot map $f : \mathbb{Z}_m \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ with $f(j+1) = f(j) + r$. Then a rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies $\mathrm{LISC}_m(L)$: winding $m$, not winding $k$. For a generator $m = k$; for $\gcd(r,k) = d > 1$ it is the strictly weaker $m = k/d$.
assumptions: Suppose the rotation $r$ closes an orbit of size $m$, witnessed by an injective slot map $f : \mathbb{Z}_m \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ with $f(j+1) = f(j) + r$.
conclusions: a rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies $\mathrm{LISC}_m(L)$: winding $m$, not winding $k$
nodes.label: lem:ng

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma NG: assembly half
nodes.statement: Read the walk through $f$: this is a rotation-$1$ witness of width $m$, so \ref{lem:assembly} assembles it. The instance $m=k$, $f = \mathrm{id}$, $r=1$ recovers Step 3. Not formalized: that the $d$ orbit cycles are pairwise vertex-disjoint.
nodes.statement_short: Read the walk through f to get a rotation-1 witness and assemble it.

nodes.name: Read through f and assemble
nodes.statement:
Read the walk through $f$: this is a rotation-$1$ witness of width $m$, so
\ref{lem:assembly} assembles it. The instance $m=k$, $f = \mathrm{id}$, $r=1$
recovers Step 3.
nodes.statement_short: Read through f and assemble

nodes.statement: Not formalized: that the $d$ orbit cycles are pairwise vertex-disjoint.

nodes.name: Eventually periodic subset of the naturals
nodes.statement: $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is eventually periodic when there are a threshold $s$ and a period $p > 0$ with $L \in S$ iff $L+p \in S$, for every $L \geq s$. Finite unions, intersections and complements are again eventually periodic, with threshold $\max$ and period $\mathrm{lcm}$.
nodes.label: def:evperiodic

nodes.name: The k-cap
nodes.statement: If $0 < L$ and $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ then $k \leq |A|$.
conclusions: $k \leq |A|$
nodes.label: lem:kcap

nodes.name: Proof of The k-cap
nodes.statement: The positions $0, L, \dots, (k-1)L$ all sit at layer $0$ and are pairwise distinct, so their states are $k$ distinct elements of $A$. Pigeonhole.
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole on the k distinct states at layer 0.

nodes.name: Unsafe and Safe
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Unsafe}(\rho)$ is the set of $L \geq 1$ with $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ for some $k \geq 2$, and $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ is its complement among the positives. Ring reconstruction $C_L = R_L$ holds exactly on $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$.
nodes.label: def:unsafe-safe

nodes.name: Unsafe is a finite union of reachability sets
nodes.statement: For finite $A$, $\mathrm{Unsafe}(\rho)$ is the union of $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}$ over $2 \leq k \leq |A|$.
conclusions: $\mathrm{Unsafe}(\rho)$ is the union of $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}$ over $2 \leq k \leq |A|$
nodes.label: lem:unsafe-biunion

nodes.name: Proof of Unsafe is a finite union of reachability sets
nodes.statement: The k-cap bounds the winding by $|A|$, making the union finite; Theorem P converts each $\mathrm{LISC}_k$ into $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: k-cap bounds the winding; Theorem P converts LISC to TR.

nodes.name: Deterministic orbits in a finite type are eventually periodic
nodes.statement: For $f : \beta \to \beta$ with $\beta$ finite and any $b$, there are $s$ and $p > 0$ with $f^{n+p}(b) = f^{n}(b)$ for all $n \geq s$.
conclusions: there are $s$ and $p > 0$ with $f^{n+p}(b) = f^{n}(b)$ for all $n \geq s$
nodes.label: lem:iterate

nodes.name: Proof of Deterministic orbits in a finite type are eventually periodic
nodes.statement: The sequence $n \mapsto f^n(b)$ cannot be injective, so it repeats; being generated deterministically, it is periodic from the first repeat onward.
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole: the orbit repeats and is periodic from the first repeat.

nodes.name: Reachability is an iterate, and matches the raw walk
nodes.statement: Length-$n$ reachability in $T_k(\rho)$ is the $n$-th iterate of a single step operator on relations over injective tuples, and it holds between $u$ and $v$ exactly when a raw tuple walk of the shape in \ref{def:tr} runs from $u$ to $v$.
conclusions: Length-$n$ reachability in $T_k(\rho)$ is the $n$-th iterate of a single step operator on relations over injective tuples
nodes.label: lem:reach-walk

nodes.name: Proof of Reachability is an iterate, and matches the raw walk
nodes.statement: Induction on $n$, rebuilding the walk one layer at a time.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on n.

nodes.name: Per-k eventual periodicity
nodes.statement: For finite $A$, the set of $L$ with $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ is eventually periodic.
conclusions: the set of $L$ with $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ is eventually periodic
nodes.label: lem:evper-tr

nodes.name: Proof of Per-k eventual periodicity
nodes.statement: The vertex set of $T_k(\rho)$ is finite, hence so is the type of relations on it; apply \ref{lem:iterate} to the step operator and transport along \ref{lem:reach-walk}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the finite-orbit periodicity to the step operator on a finite relation type.

nodes.name: Theorem B
nodes.statement: For every relation $\rho$ on a finite alphabet, $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ is eventually periodic: there are a threshold $S$ and a period $P > 0$ with $L \in \mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ iff $L+P \in \mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$, for every $L \geq S$. Membership is therefore decided by a finite table.
assumptions: For every relation $\rho$ on a finite alphabet
conclusions: $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ is eventually periodic
Membership is therefore decided by a finite table.
nodes.statement_short: For a relation on a finite alphabet, the set of safe ring lengths is eventually periodic, hence decided by a finite table.
nodes.label: thm:B

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem B
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Unsafe}$ is a finite union of eventually periodic sets by \ref{lem:unsafe-biunion} and \ref{lem:evper-tr}, hence eventually periodic with threshold the max of the thresholds and period the lcm of the periods; $\mathrm{Safe}$ is its complement among the positives.
nodes.statement_short: Unsafe is a finite union of eventually periodic sets; Safe is its complement.

nodes.name: Lemma NG, orbit-map half
nodes.statement: A rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies a simple cycle of winding $\mathrm{addOrderOf}(r) = k/\gcd(r,k)$, equal to $k$ exactly when $r$ generates.
conclusions: A rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies a simple cycle of winding $\mathrm{addOrderOf}(r) = k/\gcd(r,k)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma NG, orbit-map half
nodes.statement: The orbit map is \texttt{ZMod.lift} applied to \texttt{zmultiplesHom}, so $f(j+1) = f(j) + r$ follows from \texttt{map\_add}; injectivity is a divisibility step. Feeding this to \ref{lem:ng} gives the winding-$m$ conclusion. Still open: pairwise disjointness of the $d$ orbit cycles.
nodes.statement_short: Build the orbit map with ZMod.lift and feed it to Lemma NG.

nodes.name: Lemma NG, refutation half
nodes.statement: For the directed 4-cycle at $L = 2$ and the non-generator $r = 2$ ($\gcd(2,4) = 2$): $\mathrm{TR}_4^{(2)}(2)$ holds, $\mathrm{LISC}_2(2)$ holds, and $\mathrm{LISC}_4(2)$ \emph{fails}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma NG, refutation half
nodes.statement: The relation is a function, so every vertex of the layered ring has out-degree one and a walk is determined by its start; it returns to its starting state after four steps. A winding-4 simple cycle needs eight pairwise distinct positions, but positions $0$ and $4$ share a layer and a state. The winding-2 cycle and the rotation-2 slot walk $\tau_i(j) = j + i$ are exhibited directly. So a rotation witness at a non-generator certifies winding $k/d = 2$, not winding $k$.

nodes.statement: \ref{def:unsafe-safe} unfolds to an $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ with $k \geq 2$; apply \ref{thm:lisc-delay-witness}.
nodes.section: 7.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.statement_short: Unfold Unsafe and apply the delay-witness theorem.

nodes.name: The hypothesis is satisfiable
nodes.statement: The complete relation on $\{\bot,\top\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{LISC}_2(1)$, so the conclusion of \ref{thm:lisc-delay-witness} is inhabited.
nodes.section: 7.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
conclusions: The complete relation on $\{\bot,\top\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{LISC}_2(1)$
nodes.label: lem:lisc-inhabited

nodes.name: Proof of The hypothesis is satisfiable
nodes.statement: Steps and closure are immediate; simplicity is the two-case check that the cycle's two states differ.
nodes.section: 7.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.statement_short: Immediate steps; simplicity by a two-case check.

nodes.name: Delay queries see only non-positive times
nodes.statement: Streams agreeing at every $t \leq 0$ are indistinguishable to every delay query.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
conclusions: Streams agreeing at every $t \leq 0$ are indistinguishable to every delay query.
nodes.label: lem:delay-nonpos

nodes.name: Proof of Delay queries see only non-positive times
nodes.statement: \ref{def:delay-query} samples at $0, -\tau, \dots, -(d-1)\tau$.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
nodes.statement_short: Delay queries sample only non-positive times.

nodes.name: The two halves of a deterministic trajectory
nodes.statement: For $\omega \in \Sigma_{\mathrm{graph}(T)}$: the non-positive half is the forward orbit of the base point, $\omega(-n) = T^n(\omega_0)$; the positive half is a coherent backward orbit, $T^n(\omega_n) = \omega_0$.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
conclusions: the non-positive half is the forward orbit of the base point, $\omega(-n) = T^n(\omega_0)$
the positive half is a coherent backward orbit, $T^n(\omega_n) = \omega_0$
nodes.label: lem:graph-subshift-halves

nodes.name: Proof of The two halves of a deterministic trajectory
nodes.statement: Induction in each direction, from the trajectory condition read forwards and backwards respectively.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
nodes.statement_short: Induction in each direction from the trajectory condition.

nodes.name: Deterministic is a subclass
nodes.statement: For $\omega \in \Sigma_{\mathrm{graph}(T)}$ and an observable $h$, the delay data the relational picture assigns to $\omega$ equals the delay data the deterministic picture assigns to $\omega_0$.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
conclusions: the delay data the relational picture assigns to $\omega$ equals the delay data the deterministic picture assigns to $\omega_0$
nodes.label: thm:deterministic-subclass

nodes.name: Proof of Deterministic is a subclass
nodes.statement: Both sides evaluate at $-(k\tau)$, which \ref{lem:graph-subshift-halves} makes $T^{k\tau}(\omega_0)$.
nodes.section: 7.5.1 The deterministic case, as a subclass
nodes.statement_short: Both sides evaluate at the same point by the two-halves lemma.

nodes.name: Base points outside the subshift
nodes.statement: Being the base of a bi-infinite trajectory forces $\omega_0 \in \mathrm{range}(T^n)$ for every $n$. For non-surjective $T$ there are therefore points based at no relational trajectory whose delay data is still defined by \ref{def:orbit-stream}.
